lens: Fidelity to the brief: do charter items 1.1 to 1.4 settle what the CEO notes and the FigJam board asked, stay inside the constraints in CLAUDE.md, and log every board-versus-CLAUDE.md conflict the right way. All five files were read in full, section by section. Every file has findings; none is clean under this lens.

findings.where: Whole file (76 lines, 877 words by wc in this run)
findings.problem: Gate 1 criterion 1 in PROGRESS.md says the vision "fits on one screen", and the CEO asked for a north star that is "comprehensive yet memorable". At 877 words the file is several screens long. The north star and four horizons are buried between a rationale section, a "what it is not" section and a self-test section.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep vision.md to the north star, its three glosses and the horizons with at most three checks each, so it fits on one screen. Move "Why this is needed now", "What the system is not" and "How we will know the vision itself is useful" into a second file (for example vision-notes.md) linked from the bottom, and list it in README.md.

findings.where: A-04 table (eight rows), D-004, D-006; and charter/README.md "Status: brick (load-bearing) once Gate 1 passes"
findings.problem: Gate criterion 9 requires every board-versus-CLAUDE.md conflict to be logged under "Awaiting CEO". At least three are not. (1) The board's build flow says "Gate 1: steward reads the charter" and colours it as a human decision (notes/ceo-brief.md line 472). CLAUDE.md gives gate reviews to the lead and review of the lead's work to a fresh-context Fable reviewer, and PROGRESS.md and README.md make the charter brick on that agent-only gate. The charter defines the LOCK list, so this touches a LOCK. (2) The board has three contracts and puts "Human agency" in its tagline; CLAUDE.md lists six base values without it. The charter adds it as LOCK principle 3. This is logged as D-004 under the lead's own decisions, not under Awaiting CEO. (3) The board says "Baseline first. Set targets after observation"; CLAUDE.md asks for numeric performance budgets set in the charter. D-006 records the numbers but not the conflict. The board's "Steward picks one, or agent picks after a day" against CLAUDE.md's "visual direction: do it yourself" is also missing from A-04, although the subject belongs to item 2.1.
findings.suggestedFix: Add rows 9 to 12 to A-04. For Gate 1: say the fresh-context Fable review makes the charter the working basis for agent work, and that the LOCK list and principles stay "awaiting the steward's read" until the CEO, who holds the steward seat under A-02, has read it. Change the README status line to say the same. Move the human-agency addition from D-004 into Awaiting CEO, with the reason and how to reverse it. Record the baseline-versus-budget conflict with the resolution already in D-006.

findings.where: "Who decides what" table, rows "A change inside an ADAPT range" and "A new component or token ... with no real users affected"; Roles row "Decides everything inside ADAPT"
findings.problem: The charter gives three different answers to the board's one open policy question ("ADAPT autonomy vs human release sign-off needs an explicit boundary"). DECISIONS.md A-04 row 1 says the lead decides inside ADAPT only while no real users are affected. The ADAPT row in this table has no such condition. budget.md says "a product or an agent decides without asking". No row says who decides a non-breaking change to a part that real users already use. vision.md then promises work "without having to ask anyone" and a 5-year state where most changes are decided "without waiting for a person". A builder cannot tell whether an in-range change to a live product needs the steward.
findings.suggestedFix: State one rule and repeat it word for word in all three files. Following the board until the CEO answers: add "with no real users affected" to the ADAPT row; add a row "Any change, including one inside an ADAPT range, that reaches real users: decided by the steward"; change the budget.md sentence to "decides without asking, until the change would reach real users". In vision.md mark the 5-year autonomy bullet as depending on this boundary being agreed, and log the open boundary as its own Awaiting CEO question with the two options (steward approves every release, or steward approves a surface once and in-range changes then ship on passing checks).

findings.where: "Who decides what" table, row "A release to real users"; charter/README.md terms list; budget.md "It is clay: it is never imported by brick"
findings.problem: The board's proposed decision-rights matrix has a separate "pilot release" row, and idea N1 separates sandbox edits, pilot releases and system-wide changes. The charter has no pilot row and never defines "real user" or "pilot", although every human sign-off hangs on the phrase "reaches real users". It is also unclear whether clay or an EXPLORE variant may be shown to pilot participants: README says clay "is never shipped", yet the first pilot (E1) compares cost-summary variants with real people.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a row "Running a pilot with recruited participants": proposed by the lead, proof is the gate results plus passing LOCK checks plus safe test data, decided by the steward, rolled back by the steward, with a named rollback owner, a fallback and a stop condition recorded before it starts (board idea N5). Define "real user", "pilot participant" and "pilot" in README.md, and say that an EXPLORE variant may be shown in a pilot only when it passes every LOCK check.

findings.where: Roles row "Reviewer: A fresh subagent one tier above the builder"; "The passport": "the person or agent who writes the first part never writes the third"
findings.problem: The charter does not cover the case where the lead is the builder or proposer, which is most of the work today ("the core is the only contributor"). CLAUDE.md says the lead's own work is reviewed by a fresh-context Fable reviewer; the charter only says "one tier up", and no tier exists above Fable. The passport rule also forbids the proposer from deciding, yet the table names the lead as decider for ADAPT changes and new components. The board asks to "separate proposing from approving" and CLAUDE.md calls the third step a "human decision". For a lead proposal nobody is named to decide.
findings.suggestedFix: Add to Roles: "Work by the lead is reviewed by a fresh-context reviewer on Fable." Add to the passport: "When the lead is the proposer, the fresh-context Fable reviewer writes the proof, and the decision is recorded under Awaiting CEO as the most reversible option until a human confirms it." Say in one sentence how this squares with CLAUDE.md's "human decision": changes inside ADAPT with no real users affected are decided by the lead; everything else in the passport is a human decision.

findings.where: "How the ranking works": "If two of them appear to conflict, work stops and the steward decides"; principle 4 "Class. Meaning and behaviour are LOCK"
findings.problem: Two gaps in the ranking. (a) Conflicts among principles 1 to 3 are not settled by the ranking but passed to a steward who is not named, and "work stops" goes against CLAUDE.md's hands-off rule (choose the most reversible option, record it, continue). Gate criterion 2 says the ranking settles every conflict between two principles; on a strict reading three of the pairs are unsettled. (b) Principle 4 holds a LOCK item (semantic meaning, one of the board's four) but sits in the group that "can conflict in ordinary work" and always loses to principles 1 to 3. A builder could read that as permission to trade away a LOCK.
findings.suggestedFix: (a) Replace the sentence with: "If two of them appear to conflict, the part is not released; the lead takes the option that breaches neither, records the conflict under Awaiting CEO, and continues other work. The steward decides." (b) Add: "The LOCK part of principle 4 (meaning and behaviour) blocks release like principles 1 to 3 and is never traded. The ranking decides only the ADAPT parts of principles 4 to 7."

findings.where: "Only the steward can change a LOCK item"; against principles.md "Changing, adding or retiring a principle is the CEO's decision" and the operating-model table rows "Any change to a LOCK item" and "The principles, the ranges..."
findings.problem: Principles 1 to 3 are both principles and LOCK items. One file gives a change to them to the steward, another to the CEO, and the table has both rows. CLAUDE.md has the same overlap (steward decides any LOCK change; ask the CEO first for changes to the principles or their deltas) and the charter repeats it without settling it. It is hidden today only because the CEO holds the steward seat.
findings.suggestedFix: Settle it in the table: "A change to a LOCK item or to a principle: the steward decides and the CEO is asked first; both are recorded. A change to how a LOCK item is checked, when it tightens the check, is the lead's." Use the same sentence in budget.md and principles.md.

findings.where: "ADAPT" table as a whole; principles.md "Class. ADAPT" under principles 5, 6 and 7
findings.problem: The CEO asked that "each principle should have a range, a delta". The ADAPT table is organised by visual property and gives a reference and range only for principle 4's appearance. Principles 5, 6 and 7 are classed ADAPT but have no reference and no range anywhere, which also misses gate criterion 3 (every ADAPT item has a reference and a stated range). Their rules are written as absolutes ("nothing in brick depends on software its maker calls beta", "nothing in the core mentions a domain"), which is a zero delta, not a range. For principle 7 the ADAPT class contradicts CLAUDE.md: "nothing may be ecommerce-only unless it sits in a clearly separated domain layer".
findings.suggestedFix: Add a table "The delta for each principle" with one row per principle: its reference, its range, and the check. For 5: the counts and the performance budgets. For 6: zero beta dependencies in brick and zero breaking changes without a migration path. For 7: zero domain words in the core and zero imports from a domain layer into the core. Name these zero-tolerance rules as hard checks that fail a change in L1, and say plainly that they are not among the board's four LOCK classes, so the lead, not the steward, may revise them. Correct the Class lines in principles.md to match.

findings.where: "Accessibility (WCAG 2.2 level AA is the floor)" table
findings.problem: CLAUDE.md makes WCAG 2.2 AA the floor for every component. The table lists eleven requirements, which is a subset of level A and AA. A builder will read the table as the complete LOCK list. Criteria that matter in a checkout are absent, for example identifying input purpose so that browsers can fill in address and payment fields, announcing status messages to assistive technology, adjustable time limits, text spacing, content shown on hover or focus, and alternatives to dragging.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a final row: "Every other WCAG 2.2 level A and AA success criterion that applies to the component | A per-component audit against the full criteria list, recorded with the component". Add a sentence above the table saying that the rows are the criteria most often breached, not the whole floor. Take the criterion names and numbers from the WCAG text already checked in notes/survey, not from memory.

findings.where: "Safe behaviour" table
findings.problem: Principle 3 is a LOCK, but three clauses of its rule have no LOCK row and so no check: an action that shares data asks first (the table covers only "cannot be undone, or that spends money"); the way to reverse an action is offered wherever one exists; the system does not commit on the person's behalf. Gate criterion 3 says every LOCK item names the check that detects a breach. For an AI work assistant the last clause is the one most likely to be breached.
findings.suggestedFix: Add three rows: "An action that shares a person's data asks first and shows what will be shared | component test and review checklist"; "Where an action can be reversed, the control to reverse it is shown | component test"; "No action with consequences is taken from an inferred or ambiguous instruction | review checklist item for every flow in which the assistant acts".

findings.where: "EXPLORE": "30 days after it starts, or the end of the second build cycle of its slice, whichever comes first" and "at most one new item starts per pilot"
findings.problem: The board's idea N2 says "review after two learning cycles", meaning rounds of evidence. The charter turns this into "build cycle", which CLAUDE.md and the L2 loop define as one work item, a matter of hours. With "whichever comes first" an EXPLORE item can expire, and be "retired automatically", before any evidence from people can exist. The cap "one new item per pilot" is also undefined while no pilot can run, and principle 5 makes EXPLORE the only way to try an addition, so on a strict reading nothing can be tried at all.
findings.suggestedFix: Write: "An item is reviewed when the evidence named in it has been collected, and expires 30 days after it starts at the latest. An item whose evidence needs people does not expire while its pilot is waiting for a steward; it is marked waiting." Change the cap to "at most one new item per pilot, or per slice while no pilot is running". Define "cycle" in README.md if the word is kept.

findings.where: "ADAPT": "...are confirmed at Gate 2. After that, changing a range needs the CEO's agreement."
findings.problem: CLAUDE.md says to ask the CEO first for "changes to the principles or their deltas". The ranges are deltas and become brick at Gate 1. This sentence leaves the lead free to widen them until Gate 2, which PROGRESS.md gives to an Opus reviewer, a tier below the work it would confirm.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace with: "From Gate 1, narrowing a range is the lead's decision and widening one needs the CEO's agreement. Only the numeric steps of the scales, not the ranges, are set in phase 2."

findings.where: Principle 1, "Rule"
findings.problem: The board defines Universal as "different abilities, languages, devices and networks", and the CEO's notes say "whatever their hardware, software, language, culture, location, or physical or mental ability, including hearing, movement, sight and cognition". The rule covers abilities, devices and networks but says nothing about language, writing direction or longer translated text, and its evidence does not mention cognitive evaluation, which board idea N7 asks to track separately. A component could be built for left-to-right English only and pass every check.
findings.suggestedFix: Add to the rule: "...in a right-to-left language, and with labels translated into a language whose words are longer." Add to the L1 evidence a visual test with pseudo-translated and right-to-left text. Add to the L3 evidence that keyboard, assistive-technology and cognitive evaluation are tracked as three separate statuses. Label the new claim [pattern] or [assumption] as fits, and add it to the assumptions list.

findings.where: Principle 5, "Evidence"; operating-model.md table row "Removing or retiring a component"
findings.problem: The board's third contract names its evidence as "reuse, task success and upgrade effort", and its subtraction release ends with "Did task success hold?". Principle 5 measures only counts, shipped size and benchmark steps. Nothing in the charter checks that people still succeed after something is removed, and the removal row asks only for usage data and a migration path. The trigger "a variant unused for two releases" also depends on usage telemetry that does not exist yet, with no "not measured" note of the kind budget.md gives for design-to-code differences.
findings.suggestedFix: Add to principle 5's evidence: "how often each part is reused; the effort a product needs to upgrade; and, once people use the system, that task success held after each removal". Add to the removal row's proof: "an owner, a replacement, a migration window, a way back, and a check that task success held". State that "unused" is reported as "not measured" until usage telemetry exists.

findings.where: Principle 2, "Claims": "Unexpected extra costs are a leading reason people give for abandoning a purchase [research]"
findings.problem: The claim does not match its own reviewed source, notes/survey/checkout-evidence.md. The 40% item is "extra costs too high", which is about the amount, not about surprise; only the 12% item is about not seeing the total up front. The reviewer added that both figures exclude the 42% who were "just browsing", and said this changes how the numbers can be read; the charter omits it. "The method and sample are not public" is stronger than the survey file, which says only that no sample size is given. The claim does not point to the survey file. This principle binds the charter's own reports.
findings.suggestedFix: Rewrite: "Extra costs and not seeing the total early are among the reasons people give for abandoning a purchase [research]: Baymard Institute's list, shown as updated 28 October 2026, reports 40% for 'extra costs too high' and 12% for 'couldn't see or calculate the total up front', among shoppers who were not just browsing; the page gives no sample size. See notes/survey/checkout-evidence.md."

findings.where: "Where the system should be": headings "In 1 week", "In 1 quarter", "In 1 year", "In 5 years"
findings.problem: The CEO asked, in both the edited and the unedited voice notes, where the system should be in "1 day, 1 week, 1 year and 5 years". The vision drops 1 day and adds 1 quarter. PROGRESS.md item 1.1 does the same. The change is not recorded in DECISIONS.md.
findings.suggestedFix: Add an "In 1 day" horizon with checks an outsider can observe (for example: the charter drafts exist and have each had a fresh-context review; the conflicts and unfilled placeholders are logged; nothing has reached a real user). Keep the quarter if it is useful, and log in DECISIONS.md that a fifth horizon was added.

findings.where: "North star" and "In 1 year": "costs no more to maintain than it did with one"
findings.problem: CLAUDE.md and the board both name the north star as universal, unified and scalable, and CLAUDE.md defines each. None of the three words appears in the vision, so the CEO cannot see their own goal in it. The 1-year headline also overstates the definition of scalable ("without matching growth in maintenance" becomes "costs no more"), and none of the five checks under it measures maintenance cost, so the claim that defines scalability has no check.
findings.suggestedFix: Add one line under the north star: "Every surface is universal. The same promises is unified: one source and zero drift. Whoever builds it is scalable: hundreds of products without matching growth in maintenance." Change the 1-year headline to "its maintenance cost grows more slowly than the number of products" and add a check from the scorecard, for example cost per component and cost per release at three products compared with one.

findings.where: "Why this is needed now": "used to appear a few times a quarter. At machine speed it can appear many times a day, and each one makes the next more likely"; "If there are two sets of docs, they will drift apart, and agents will follow the wrong one"
findings.problem: These are claims about how people and agents behave. They carry no [research], [pattern] or [assumption] label, which CLAUDE.md and gate criterion 8 require, and the first two give frequencies that nothing supports. The sentence "not a measured rate" admits this but does not replace the label.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove the frequencies: "A difference that nobody decided on appears more often when more builders work faster [assumption]." Label the two-sets-of-docs sentence [pattern] and point to the survey file that supports it, or label it [assumption]. Add both to the assumptions list.

findings.where: "The four loops" table, L1 "Actuator: Fix and rerun"; "Who decides what" table
findings.problem: CLAUDE.md says "Do not loosen or delete a test to make a check pass" and lists what the lead may change alone: skills, briefs, docs, lint rules, the work tree, and tests only when adding or tightening. Neither rule is in the charter. "Fix and rerun" does not rule out fixing the check, and the table has no row for a change to a test, a lint rule, a skill or a brief.
findings.suggestedFix: Change the L1 actuator to "Fix the change and rerun; a check is never loosened or deleted to make it pass". Add two rows: "Adding or tightening a test or lint rule; changing a skill, brief, docs page or the work tree: decided by the lead" and "Loosening or removing a test or lint rule: CEO is asked first".

findings.where: "No standing committee of agents": "The viewpoints are: a person using assistive technology..."
findings.problem: An agent asked to take the viewpoint of "a person using assistive technology" can be mistaken for evidence about such people. The board says "Test with people; do not infer their needs from agent agreement" and CLAUDE.md says "You are not human".
findings.suggestedFix: Rename the viewpoint to "an accessibility specialist checking against WCAG and known assistive-technology behaviour" and add: "What these reviewers say about people is labelled [pattern] or [assumption]; it is never recorded as evidence from users."

findings.where: "The four loops" table, row "Current state", L2 "Running informally from this commit"; "The human review queue"
findings.problem: Three small gaps against CLAUDE.md's "Feedback loops" section. (1) The L2 variable is the scorecard and the benchmark score, but no benchmark tasks exist yet (item 1.6 is "next"), so "running" claims more than can be shown. (2) The human queue is described but not given the seven fields CLAUDE.md asks for each loop; it has no owner, no desired state and no named reviewers. (3) budget.md says an out-of-range value "is either pulled back, or becomes an EXPLORE item", while this file says a liked item becomes a proposal to widen the range or to promote it. Neither says what happens while the queue has no reviewers.
findings.suggestedFix: (1) Write "Review one tier up is running. The benchmark is not written, so there is no score yet." (2) Add the queue as a fifth column or a small table with variable, current state, desired state, sensor, actuator, owner and cadence. (3) Use one sentence in both files and add the default: "With no vote after seven days, or while the queue has no reviewers, the item is pulled back to the reference."

findings.where: "Team model" table and the paragraph under it; "Recruiting and retiring subagents"
findings.problem: The CEO asked for the pros and cons of each team model and named a fourth option: a hybrid of a central team plus humans who contribute. The table gives only why each was not chosen alone and does not say that the choice is that hybrid. Four CEO questions that belong to this item have no answer: whether principles are decided first and then validated or validated by recruits; whether the work runs in one chat or nested chats; what the lead needs from the CEO (only DECISIONS.md A-02 says); and how a subagent asks when it does not understand, given the CEO's note that agents "should look for information and ask". Separately, "a federated model rarely succeeds without a central team" understates the reviewed source: notes/survey/thinkers.md corrected exactly this wording to say Curtis reports no such case among more than 80 systems.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a "Strength" column and a "Hybrid" row marked as the choice. Add a short "Questions the CEO asked" list with a one-sentence answer each, including "A subagent that cannot complete its brief from the sources says so and asks the lead; it does not guess" and a pointer to A-02 for resources. Change the Curtis sentence to "He later wrote that he had seen no federated system succeed without investment in a central team."

findings.where: "Rams:" line under each principle; "Alternatives considered"
findings.problem: CLAUDE.md asks for Rams' ten principles as a lens. Seven are each quoted once and the others (aesthetic, environmentally friendly, and useful and understandable merged into one) are not accounted for; "innovative" for principle 7 is a loose fit. The CEO also offered candidate principles ("be unique, honourable and delightful; build confidence through consistency and transparency; nail the basics; clear choices and context") and the file does not say what became of them.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a ten-row table: each Rams principle, where it lands (a principle, the budget, or a later item such as visual direction), or "not used, because...". Add two sentences to "Alternatives considered" saying which of the CEO's candidates were absorbed and where, and which were left to voice and visual direction.

findings.where: "In 1 quarter" bullets; "In 5 years": "what is worth exploring"; end of file
findings.problem: (1) The quarter checks need a steward and participants that only the CEO can supply; the vision does not say so, although the CEO asked "what are the resources you need from me". (2) "A second product surface outside checkout" should be appointment booking, built only after checkout passes and part by part (CLAUDE.md and A-04 row 6). (3) The 5-year state says people decide "what is worth exploring", but the operating model lets the lead start an EXPLORE item. (4) The file records no alternative north stars and no counterargument, although CLAUDE.md asks for at least three variants where taste is involved and principles.md does this.
findings.suggestedFix: (1) Add under the quarter heading: "These checks depend on a named steward and on people to test with; see DECISIONS.md A-02." (2) Write "Appointment booking has been built from the parts that have evidence, after checkout passed". (3) Change to "what is promoted from exploration". (4) Add three lines listing the north-star variants considered and the strongest argument against the chosen one; these can live in the notes file proposed in the first finding.

findings.where: Header "Altitude: system"; Accessibility row "every declared text and background token pair"; "Performance budgets" first paragraph
findings.problem: (1) The board places "the budget and patterns at the pattern level"; the header says system. (2) Checking only "declared" pairs leaves a gap: a pair a component uses but nobody declared is never checked, while CLAUDE.md makes AA the floor for every token pair. (3) The CEO asked to test "early and often on real devices, real hardware, real networks". The budgets are lab-only, which is stated honestly, but the file does not say when real-device measurement starts, and the "simulated mid-range phone on a slow 4G connection" has no numbers, so two runs may not be comparable.
findings.suggestedFix: (1) Either change the altitude to patterns or add one sentence saying why the lead placed it at system. (2) Add: "A lint check fails when a component uses a text and background pair that is not declared." (3) Add: "Real-device measurement starts with the first pilot and needs devices from the CEO. The lab profile's processor slowdown and network speeds are fixed in item 4.1 and recorded here."

findings.where: Terms: "Benchmark: three fixed build tasks given to a less capable agent"
findings.problem: CLAUDE.md fixes the benchmark as "three fixed ecommerce build tasks" and A-04 row 7 keeps it that way. The definition drops "ecommerce", which blurs the open question in A-05 about adding a booking task.
findings.suggestedFix: Write "three fixed ecommerce build tasks given to a Sonnet or Haiku agent that has only the published docs".

findings.where: A-01: "Those remarks were removed from the survey files"
findings.problem: This is outside the five charter files; it was found while checking a citation. notes/survey/checkout-evidence.md line 52 still says "the repo's 32px is stricter", a remark taken from the retired AGENTS.md. The claim in A-01 is therefore not true as written, which matters under CLAUDE.md's clean-slate and honesty rules. None of the five charter files carries the leak.
findings.suggestedFix: Delete that clause from the survey file, search notes/survey for other such remarks, and change A-01 to state what was checked and when.

strongestCounterargument: The charter is more faithful to the board's governance model than to what the CEO asked for, and it hardens untested proposals into load-bearing rules by a route the board itself rejects. The board labels every part of its model as proposed, untested and not adopted, says "agent consensus is not user research", and puts a human at Gate 1 ("steward reads the charter"). The charter takes those proposals, adds numbers the lead chose (three active experiments, 30 days, the ranges, the byte budgets), and declares the result brick after a review by another agent of the same model, with no steward named and nobody to test with. Its central promise, that the system is "corrected by evidence from people", cannot be kept or broken for as long as that stays true: two of the four loops, every "on every pilot" evidence line and the whole 1-quarter horizon are dormant. Meanwhile the CEO's stated wants are a working system to react to, not a plan; a lead who owns the system now; and humans brought in later. Under that reading a more faithful charter would be much shorter, would make brick only what a machine can check today, and would mark everything that needs a person as clay that is explicitly waiting, instead of presenting an eleven-thousand-word governance design as settled before a single token exists.

lens: The sceptic: try to prove charter items 1.1 to 1.4 wrong before the gate does. All five files were read in full, every section. Reference material consulted (not reviewed): PROGRESS.md gate criteria, CLAUDE.md, DECISIONS.md, notes/survey/checkout-evidence.md, notes/survey/thinkers.md, notes/sources/2026-11-13-figjam-board.md. No file was written and no git command was run. Verdict is "fail as drafted": three explicit Gate 1 pass criteria (1, 2 and 10) are not met as written. All three are cheap edits; the majors below are the more serious work.

findings.where: Whole file, against Gate 1 criterion 1 in PROGRESS.md: "It fits on one screen."
findings.problem: The file is 877 words and 77 source lines. Under any ordinary reading that is two to three screens on a laptop and more on a phone. The criterion was written before the phase started, so the gate reviewer has to mark it unmet. "One screen" is also not defined anywhere, so nobody can show it is met.
findings.suggestedFix: Cut the vision to what fits one screen: the north star line with its three glosses, one line per horizon with its single most observable check, and the "is not" list. Move the full horizon checklists to a second section or file called "Horizon checks". State the size you mean (for example "at most 300 words above the first rule line") so the criterion can be checked. Do not relax the criterion to make the draft pass.

findings.where: "How the ranking works": "They do not trade against each other. If two of them appear to conflict, work stops and the steward decides."
findings.problem: Gate 1 criterion 2 says "The ranking settles every conflict between two principles." For principles 1, 2 and 3 the ranking settles nothing: it hands the conflict to a steward, and operating-model.md says no steward is named. "Work stops" also contradicts the hands-off rule the lead works under (take the most reversible option, log it, continue). The claim that the three never trade is asserted, not shown, and the first slice already contains real conflicts: (a) principle 3 keeps what a person entered after an error, while the Safe behaviour LOCK in budget.md says payment details are not kept longer than the task needs; (b) principle 3 asks for a confirmation before every action that spends money or shares data, and each extra step is a cost to people using a screen reader or switch access under principle 1; (c) principle 2 adds disclosures, and more text works against people with cognitive disabilities under principle 1.
findings.suggestedFix: Give the first group a rule that settles a conflict without a person: "If a design cannot keep all three, it is not shipped; the lead picks the most reversible design that breaches none, logs the conflict under Awaiting CEO, and other work continues." Add a tie-break order for the rare case where no such design exists (for example 1, then 2, then 3) and say the steward may overturn it. Then work the three conflicts above as examples so a builder can see the rule applied.

findings.where: "Terms used in the charter", against Gate 1 criterion 10: "Every special term is defined where it first appears or in charter/README.md."
findings.problem: Many terms are used in the four files and defined neither at first use nor here. Never defined in any of the five files: pilot; scorecard; baseline; primitive, semantic and component tokens (vision says only "three layers"); work item; build cycle; theme file; vocabulary file; declared pair; design source; subagent; brief; skill; the approvals list; sandbox channel; digest; phase 2 and phase 4; "the board" and "FigJam board"; "the brief"; "Rams"; CLAUDE.md; Item 1.1 to 1.4. Used before they are defined, given the stated reading order: L1, L2, L3, L4 (all through principles.md, defined only in operating-model.md); lead and CEO (used in principles.md and budget.md before the roles table); human review queue (vision.md). Unexplained technical terms: WCAG 2.2 level AA; largest contentful paint, interaction to next paint, cumulative layout shift; sensor, actuator and variable in the loops table. The Tier entry lists Sonnet, Haiku, Opus and Fable without saying they are AI models.
findings.suggestedFix: Add each term above to this list in one plain sentence, in the order a reader meets them. For L1 to L4 add one line each ("L1, the change loop: the automated checks run on every change" and so on). For the three web measures give a plain gloss ("how long until the main content is visible", "how long the page takes to respond to a tap", "how much the page jumps while loading"). Replace "the board" with "the CEO's planning board (a FigJam file, summarised in notes/sources/)" and "the brief" with "the CEO's written brief (CLAUDE.md)". Add "Rams: Dieter Rams, an industrial designer whose ten principles of good design are used here as a cross-check."

findings.where: "Status: brick (load-bearing) once Gate 1 passes."
findings.problem: Gate 1 is a review by a fresh agent on the same model as the author. So the principles, the LOCK list and every number become load-bearing without any person having read them, and after that only the steward or CEO may change them. The rule for changing them is stricter than the process that made them. The board summary in notes/sources/2026-11-13-figjam-board.md describes Gate 1 as "the steward reads it and it passes or is revised"; the work tree says a fresh Fable reviewer. That difference touches the LOCK list and is not among the eight conflicts logged in DECISIONS.md A-04, which puts Gate 1 criterion 9 at risk. (I read the summary, not the board itself.)
findings.suggestedFix: Change the status line to: "Brick for agent work once Gate 1 passes. No person has approved it. The principles, the LOCK list and the ranges stay provisional until the CEO, who holds the steward seat, has read them." Log the Gate 1 difference as a ninth board conflict under Awaiting CEO.

findings.where: Terms list: "Drift", "LOCK", "Benchmark"
findings.problem: Three definitions do not match their use. Drift is defined here as a difference "that nobody decided on", but budget.md counts every raw value and every second implementation, decided or not. LOCK is defined as a delta, but principles.md uses it as a class of principle ("Principles 1 to 3 are LOCK items"). Benchmark is described in the present tense although its tasks and the published docs do not exist yet.
findings.suggestedFix: Pick one drift definition and use it in both files. Define LOCK as "a requirement whose delta must be zero". Write "Benchmark: three fixed build tasks that will be given to..." until the first run exists.

findings.where: North star: "Every surface keeps the same promises, whoever builds it."
findings.problem: Strongest honest argument against the line. (1) It describes conformity to rules the system wrote for itself, not an outcome for people. Every surface could keep all seven promises while people still fail at their tasks, and the line would be satisfied. The board's own tagline included "Evidence-led evolution"; the line drops it, although point 3 of "Why this is needed now" says evidence from people must be able to change the principles. (2) It fails the file's own usefulness test. It cannot settle which surface to build next or what to leave out, and almost nothing could "fall outside it", so the second review question can never be answered yes. (3) Only principles 1 to 3 are promises to a person. "Less", "Built to last" and "Composed" are rules for maintainers; a surface does not "keep" them. (4) The CEO asked for universal, unified and scalable. The line covers the first two and says nothing about maintenance not growing with the number of products. (5) "Without having to ask anyone" is contradicted by principles.md ("work stops and the steward decides") and by operating-model.md, where the lead decides changes inside ADAPT.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep the line if you wish, but record this argument in the decision log and repair the gaps in the glosses: say the promises to people are principles 1 to 3 and that 4 to 7 are how the system keeps them; add a fourth gloss, "The promises change when evidence from people shows they are wrong"; and change "without having to ask anyone" to "without asking anyone, for anything inside the written ranges". Add one sentence on what the line rules out, so it can settle an argument.

findings.where: "What the system is not": "It is not a plan. It is working software and working guidance, checked on every change."
findings.problem: This states in the present tense that working software exists and is checked on every change. Today the repository holds no token, no component and no check; operating-model.md says the change loop is "Not running". A newcomer reading this sentence would believe the system exists. The same slip is in point 1 of "Why this is needed now": "Each promise is written as a contract with a check"; the contracts are written, the checks are not.
findings.suggestedFix: Write: "It is not meant to stay a plan. Today it is a charter and nothing else. The aim is working software and working guidance, checked on every change." In point 1 write "Each promise is written as a contract, and each contract names the check that will be built for it."

findings.where: "Why this is needed now": "A difference that nobody decided on used to appear a few times a quarter. At machine speed it can appear many times a day, and each one makes the next more likely." and "If there are two sets of docs, they will drift apart, and agents will follow the wrong one."
findings.problem: These are claims about how people and agents behave, and none carries a label, which Gate 1 criterion 8 requires. "A few times a quarter" and "many times a day" are frequencies nobody measured; the disclaimer that follows does not remove them. "Each one makes the next more likely" is a causal claim with no source. "Will drift apart" and "will follow the wrong one" are predictions stated as certainties. "Three things that older systems did not have to do" is also a claim about other systems that the survey does not support: several public systems already publish lint rules and agent-readable docs.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove both frequencies. Write: "When agents build, differences nobody decided on can appear faster than people can review them [assumption]: we have no measured rate, and the drift count on the scorecard will give one." Label the two-docs sentence [assumption] and change "will" to "are likely to". Change "that older systems did not have to do" to "that matter more when agents build".

findings.where: "In 1 quarter" and "In 1 year" (heading sentence: "costs no more to maintain than it did with one")
findings.problem: (1) The one-year headline is the CEO's scalability goal, and no check beneath it measures maintenance cost. The five bullets could all be true while cost triples. (2) Three of the five one-quarter checks need people who do not exist: a steward, test participants and queue reviewers. "None of them has been met yet" does not tell the reader that the lead cannot meet them alone. (3) "One release has removed more than it added" in the first quarter of a four-part system invites adding things in order to remove them. (4) "The benchmark score has held or improved at every release" rewards tuning the docs to three fixed tasks. (5) "The human review queue has received votes" is met by a single vote.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a one-year check: "Cost per component and maintenance effort per product, as recorded on the scorecard, are no higher with three products than with one." Mark each one-quarter check that needs a person with "needs: a named steward and participants; not in the lead's control". Replace the subtraction check with "the first removal review has been held and its result recorded, even if it removed nothing". Give the queue check a count and a named reviewer group.

findings.where: "How we will know the vision itself is useful"
findings.problem: The rewrite rule punishes success. If the vision is clear and everybody follows it, no disagreement arises, the answer to the first question is "no" for two quarters, and the vision is rewritten. Also "1 week" is stated with no start date, so an outsider cannot check it.
findings.suggestedFix: Change the first question to "Was the vision used to make or refuse at least one decision this quarter, and can we point to it?" Give the horizons dates counted from Gate 1.

findings.where: "3. The person decides, even over the system being helpful", "Class. LOCK", and the row "Universality | 1, and 3" / "Honesty | 2, and 3" in "Coverage of the base values"
findings.problem: Strongest honest argument against locking principle 3. (1) It is not one of the CEO's six base values. It comes from a tagline on a board where nothing is approved. The coverage table presents it as "honesty and universality together", which hides that a seventh value was added. Once locked, it outranks four of the CEO's own values, including unity and scalability, two of the three headline goals. The addition is logged as a lead decision (D-004), not under Awaiting CEO. (2) A LOCK needs a yes-or-no check. "The person stays in control of anything with consequences" has none. The checkable parts are already the Safe behaviour LOCK in budget.md, which is what the CEO's brief names. (3) The two files lock different things: this rule also covers actions that share data and requires an offered way to reverse; the budget.md table has neither. A builder cannot tell which is the LOCK. (4) Souvenir is an AI work assistant. "It does not commit on the person's behalf" at zero tolerance forbids standing permissions and scheduled or delegated actions. That is a product strategy decision made inside a design-system rule. The 5-year vision gives the system's own agents exactly this delegated freedom inside written ranges while denying it to users. (5) A confirmation before every action that spends money or shares data may train people to approve without reading [assumption], which would weaken the control the principle is meant to protect.
findings.suggestedFix: Lock only the checkable behaviours and make the two files list the same ones: input survives an error; no double submit; a destructive action is never the default; an action that cannot be undone, spends money or shares data asks first; a reversible action offers its undo. Keep "the person decides" as the principle these serve. Add a written range for delegation: a person may authorise the system in advance, within limits the person set, shown to them, and revocable; anything outside is a breach. Name human agency as an added seventh value in the coverage table, and log the addition and the delegation question under Awaiting CEO.

findings.where: "How the ranking works" and "Alternatives considered"
findings.problem: Strongest honest argument against seven principles in two groups. (1) Strict priority between groups means any small gain for group one beats any cost to group two. Every extra disclosure or confirmation wins over "Less", so clutter accumulates by rule. (2) The order 4, 5, 6, 7 has no stated reason, and scalability, the CEO's stated reason for the system, is last. (3) Principles 4 and 5 deadlock: 4 says a new pattern goes into the system and never into product code; 5 says the default answer to an addition is no and the need must have appeared more than once. A product with a first-time need can do neither. The four checkout parts themselves fail the "appeared more than once" test. (4) Principle 5 says EXPLORE is "the only way to try an addition", while operating-model.md lets the lead approve a new component directly. (5) Principle 4 is partly LOCK but sits in the group that "can conflict in ordinary work", and the text says only principles 1 to 3 are LOCK items. (6) Principles 2 and 3 overlap as written: "no choice made for the person in advance" is a control rule placed under truth. (7) The three alternatives varied only the framing. None had fewer principles, although the board proposes three contracts and the file itself admits 5, 6 and 7 may overlap. Seven is the maximum the work tree allows.
findings.suggestedFix: Give one sentence of reasoning for each step of the order 4 over 5 over 6 over 7, or change the order. State what a product does with a first-time need (compose from existing parts; if that fails, an EXPLORE item; on the second occurrence, into the system) and exempt the first slice in words. Make principle 5 and the decision table agree on how an addition enters. Say plainly that the LOCK part of principle 4 never trades. Move pre-selected options to principle 3. Add a fourth alternative with four or five principles (for example 5 and 6 merged) and say why it lost, or adopt it.

findings.where: Triggers of principles 1, 2 and 3: "Any barrier that stops a person completing a task", "A total a person cannot state", "A person who needs help to recover. Action: release is blocked."
findings.problem: These put a zero-tolerance LOCK on outcomes measured with people. As written, one participant in one session who needs help, or who cannot state the total, blocks release. That is a 100 percent target set before any baseline, which breaks the rule "baseline before targets" and Gate 1 criterion 8 ("Targets come after baselines"). It also contradicts the pilot loop in operating-model.md, whose desired state is "at or above the baseline". The file mixes two different kinds of evidence under one class: machine checks, where zero is meaningful, and human sessions, where it is not.
findings.suggestedFix: Split each trigger in two. Machine-checked breach: release is blocked, zero tolerance. Evidence from people: "a result below the baseline, or a barrier seen in a session, goes to the steward, who decides approve, revise or retire." State that no pass mark for people is set until the baseline has been measured.

findings.where: Principle 2, "Claims": "Unexpected extra costs are a leading reason people give for abandoning a purchase [research]"
findings.problem: The [research] label does not support the sentence as worded. Per notes/survey/checkout-evidence.md the Baymard item is "Extra costs too high", which is about the amount, not about surprise. Only the 12 percent item is about not seeing the total. The sentence also leaves out two limits the survey reviewer added because they change how the numbers read: the percentages exclude the 42 percent of shoppers who were "just browsing", and the respondents are US online shoppers reporting their own reasons. The full study sits behind a "/premium/" link and appears to be paywalled, the page was read through a summarising tool, and the citation has no link. The claim does not rest on an item the survey marks "(not verified)", and the charter does say the method and sample are not public.
findings.suggestedFix: Reword to what the source says: "In Baymard Institute's survey of US online shoppers (list shown as updated 28 October 2026), among those who meant to buy, 40% gave 'extra costs too high' and 12% gave not being able to see or calculate the total up front as a reason for abandoning [research: self-reported; method and sample not public; the full study appears to be paywalled; read through a summarising tool]. Source: https://baymard.com/lists/cart-abandonment-rate, notes in notes/survey/checkout-evidence.md." Label "the cost was unexpected" as [assumption].

findings.where: Principle 3, "Claims": "public guidance from GOV.UK, Nielsen Norman Group and Baymard agrees"
findings.problem: The sentence joins two claims and overstates the agreement. On keeping valid input, notes/survey/checkout-evidence.md records only GOV.UK ("never clear fields"); it records the Nielsen Norman Group article as "silent on preserving input", and the Baymard article is about when to validate. The [pattern] label is right for "explain the error next to the field", but three sources do not agree on "keep valid input".
findings.suggestedFix: Split it: "Explaining the error next to the field helps people recover [pattern]: GOV.UK, Nielsen Norman Group and Baymard guidance agree; no controlled study found. Keeping valid input helps people recover [pattern]: GOV.UK guidance only; WCAG 2.2 criterion 3.3.7 requires it but is a rule, not evidence."

findings.where: Principle 4 (no "Claims" paragraph) and principle 1 (no "Claims" paragraph)
findings.problem: Principle 4 rests on a claim about people that is not stated or labelled: that people recognise the same meaning when appearance varies between themes and densities. The board lists this as hypothesis H3, "AI-proposed, untested". It is missing from "Assumptions that need a human test". Principle 1 has an assumption in that list (number 5) but no Claims paragraph, so the file's own format is not followed. Principle 1's title also promises more than its rule checks: "everyone" has no check for language (translated text, text that grows, right-to-left scripts) or for cognition, both of which the CEO's notes and the board name. And its rule includes "a slow connection and a low-end phone" while principle 5 says the performance budgets belong to it, so a builder cannot tell whether performance is LOCK or ADAPT.
findings.suggestedFix: Add to principle 4: "Claims. People recognise the same meaning and behaviour across themes and densities [assumption]: the board's third hypothesis, untested." Add it to the assumptions list. Add a Claims paragraph to principle 1. In principle 1, either add language and cognitive checks to the rule and evidence, or add: "Not yet covered: languages other than English, right-to-left scripts, cognitive accessibility. The title is the aim, not the current coverage." Say in one place whether a performance breach is LOCK (principle 1) or ADAPT (principle 5).

findings.where: Every "Evidence" paragraph, and principle 5 "Claims": "the benchmark measures this for agents"
findings.problem: The Evidence paragraphs are in the present tense ("the automated accessibility scan, the keyboard path test and the contrast check pass"; "Nightly: the scan finds no second implementation"). None of these checks exists. The file never says so; only the loops table in operating-model.md does. "The benchmark measures this for agents" is wrong twice: the benchmark has not run, and three fixed tasks at one number of options cannot show that fewer options make correct use easier, because nothing is compared.
findings.suggestedFix: Add under "Status": "No check named in this file exists yet. Each Evidence paragraph says what will be collected once the check is built; until then the rule is enforced by review only." Change the principle 5 sentence to: "The benchmark will show how well a less capable agent builds from the docs; it does not compare more options with fewer, so this stays an assumption for agents as well as people."

findings.where: "What makes a principle useful, and when one is retired": "it decided nothing in the quarter" and "Changing, adding or retiring a principle is the CEO's decision."
findings.problem: (1) The retirement test applies to the three LOCK principles too. A LOCK that everyone obeys produces no disagreement, so "it decided nothing in the quarter" would mark "Usable by everyone" for rewriting because it worked. "Evidence from people contradicts it" could be read to retire accessibility if most participants prefer a pointer-only design. (2) Decision rights conflict: here the CEO changes any principle; budget.md says "Only the steward can change a LOCK item"; operating-model.md gives LOCK changes to the steward and principles to the CEO. Principles 1 to 3 are both. The conflict is hidden today only because the CEO holds both seats.
findings.suggestedFix: Exempt principles 1 to 3 from the "decided nothing" test and say what counts for them instead (breaches caught and blocked, or none attempted). State that evidence from people can change how a LOCK principle is met but cannot retire it without the CEO. Write one rule in all three files: "A change to principles 1 to 3 or to any LOCK item needs both the CEO and the steward."

findings.where: The "Rams:" line under each principle; "seven is at the top of the allowed range"
findings.problem: The notes in notes/survey/thinkers.md record four of Rams's sentences as checked. The glosses used for principles 3, 6 and 7 (unobtrusive, long-lasting, innovative) are paraphrases of text the notes did not record, and "leaves room for the person's own choices" shifts the meaning towards principle 3. Pairing "Composed, even over custom" with "innovative" is forced. "The allowed range" is not explained: a newcomer does not know that the work tree asked for five to seven.
findings.suggestedFix: Check the three glosses against the cited page and mark each as a paraphrase, or quote exactly. For principle 7 write "Rams: no close match" if that is the honest answer. Write "seven is the most the work plan allows (it asked for five to seven)".

findings.where: "LOCK: the delta must be zero", column "Check that detects a breach"; and "What 'zero drift' means": "The first two are counted by lint on every change and by the nightly scan."
findings.problem: Every check is named in the present tense as if it runs. No lint, test, scan, vocabulary file or reference checkout page exists. The file has no sentence saying so. "All are measured in a lab" in "Performance budgets" has the same fault: nothing has been measured.
findings.suggestedFix: Add below the title: "Nothing in this file is enforced by a machine yet. Each check named here is built in phases 2 to 4. Until a check exists, its row is enforced by review, and the scorecard reports it as 'not measured', not as zero." Change "are measured" to "will be measured" and "are counted" to "will be counted".

findings.where: "Truthful content" table, and the rows whose check is "Review checklist item"
findings.problem: Several LOCK rows name a check that cannot detect the breach. A writing check cannot know whether "Only 2 left" is true; that depends on stock data, and it is principle 2's own example. A component test shows that a "Saved" state can be drawn, not that the product shows it only after the save finished. A test on the cost summary cannot know whether the product passed in every charge. These are properties of a product's data and flow, which the design system does not own, so the system promises a zero it cannot sense. Five rows rest only on a "review checklist item" (colour alone, re-entry, machine-made content, sensitive values, flows), with no named reviewer; that is an opinion, while the file says "A delta is a fact that a check can report".
findings.suggestedFix: Add a column "What the system can check" and "What the product must prove". For each truthful-content row say which half the component enforces (for example: the cost summary cannot be rendered without a total and a list of charges) and which half is a release condition the product signs in its passport. For checklist rows, name who runs the checklist and mark the row "judged by review, not measured".

findings.where: "Accessibility (WCAG 2.2 level AA is the floor)" table
findings.problem: (1) The heading says all of WCAG 2.2 AA is the floor, but the table lists eleven requirements. Criteria the survey notes list for checkout are absent, such as identifying input purpose (1.3.5), status messages (4.1.3) and accessible authentication (3.3.8). A builder will read the table as the whole LOCK. (2) "No interactive target is smaller than 24 by 24 pixels" drops the exceptions WCAG gives; a link inside a sentence of 16 pixel text is shorter than 24 pixels, so at zero tolerance every inline link blocks release. (3) "A person is never asked to re-enter information" also drops WCAG's exceptions, so a confirm-password field or a repeated security code is a breach.
findings.suggestedFix: State: "Every WCAG 2.2 level A and AA criterion is LOCK. The table lists the ones with a dedicated check; the rest are covered by the scan and the named manual check." Add the missing checkout criteria as rows. For target size, adopt the WCAG exceptions in words or state how inline links comply. For re-entry, add "except where repeating it is essential or needed for security".

findings.where: "Safe behaviour" table against "Performance budgets": "JavaScript needed to read the page and complete the core task | None"
findings.problem: Two pairs of rules collide in the first slice. (1) "Valid input survives an error" against "Payment details and other sensitive values are never kept in the page longer than the task needs": after a failed payment, is the card number kept or cleared? Both are LOCK, and principles.md says a LOCK conflict stops work. Payment rules may also forbid keeping the security code [assumption: check the card-industry standard before deciding]. (2) "A second press of a submit control does not submit twice" is checked by "Component test on the button", but with no JavaScript a button cannot prevent a second press; only the server can. The same applies to moving focus to an error and announcing a status. The zero-JavaScript budget moves LOCK behaviour to servers the design system does not own, and the named component test cannot pass honestly.
findings.suggestedFix: Decide and write the card case: for example "all valid input is kept after an error except the card security code, which is cleared and the person is told why". For the JavaScript budget, state what the page does without script (a full round trip to the server) and what the server must guarantee (one order per submission), and change the check to "component test with script; documented server requirement without script". If that is too weak for a LOCK, allow a small script for the core task and say so.

findings.where: "ADAPT" table and the sentence "The 44 pixel control height, the 16 pixel text floor and the 45 to 75 character measure are inferred from established patterns in public guidelines."
findings.problem: Are the numbers justified? Mostly not shown. (1) No guideline is named. The notes support 44 only as Apple's hit region in points, not CSS pixels and not height alone; charter/survey.md still lists the touch-target floor as an open question. The notes support 16 pixels only for text in inputs, not body text. I found no source in notes/ for 45 to 75 characters. (2) The measure cannot be met on the system's main target. At 320 pixels wide and 16 pixel text a line holds roughly 35 to 40 characters (my estimate from the rule of thumb that an average character is about half the font size wide; it should be measured). Every phone page would fall below 45 and be sent to the review queue. (3) "Any hue" for the accent lets a product choose red, which collides with the danger colour and with principle 4. (4) Density says both "three named steps" and a multiplier "0.75 to 1.25"; a builder cannot tell whether 0.9 is allowed. The 44 pixel rule covers only "primary controls". (5) Motion says a product "may shorten durations" and also allows "0 to 500 milliseconds"; it is unclear whether a product may lengthen. (6) The multiplier of 0 to 2 for shape, 0.75 to 1.25 for density and 500 milliseconds have no stated basis.
findings.suggestedFix: Name the guideline for each number with a link to the survey note, or mark it "[assumption] the lead's starting value". Settle the touch-target question in the survey before this file uses 44. Change the measure to "at most 75 characters; no minimum on narrow screens". Add "the accent must be distinguishable from every status colour" with a check. Choose either named steps or a continuous range for density and apply the 44 pixel rule to every control on touch screens, or explain why not. Write "a product may shorten but not lengthen; the system's own durations are at most 500 milliseconds".

findings.where: "Performance budgets" table and the paragraph beginning "The last three thresholds"
findings.problem: (1) The byte budgets are guesses, and the file says so, but the rules around them make a guess hard to correct: tightening needs nobody, loosening needs the CEO. If the first build is over 12 kilobytes, every change fails until a hands-off CEO acts. The file says only what happens when the first build is under. Tightening to "measured plus a tenth" after the first build leaves almost no room for later accessibility fixes. "Well under" is not defined. Setting targets before a baseline also breaks the lead's own rule. (2) "Compressed" does not say with which method, so the number cannot be checked. (3) "A simulated mid-range phone on a slow 4G connection" gives no processor slowdown, bandwidth, delay or tool, so two honest runs will disagree. (4) The three timing limits are Google's published "good" thresholds, which Google defines for real-user data at the 75th percentile; here they are applied to a lab run. No file in notes/ records where the thresholds were checked. Response-to-tap time means little on a page with no script. (5) A page of at most 100 kilobytes with no script and system fonts is likely to show its main content far sooner than 2.5 seconds, so that limit would not catch a regression; the tightening rule covers only the byte budgets. (6) It is not stated whether the 100 kilobytes includes a substituted web font.
findings.suggestedFix: Label the byte rows "[starting guess, not measured]". Add: "At Gate 3 the lead resets each budget once to the first measured value plus a stated margin, up or down, and logs it; after that, loosening needs the CEO." Name the compression method. Write the lab profile as numbers and name the tool. Cite the page for the three thresholds and state that they are lab stand-ins for field thresholds. Extend the tightening rule to the timing limits. Say whether fonts count toward the page total.

findings.where: "EXPLORE: outside the range, for a limited time": expiry and "Limits"
findings.problem: The mechanism cannot work today and its numbers are guesses presented as rules. (1) Expiry is "30 days ... or the end of the second build cycle of its slice, whichever comes first". operating-model.md says a build cycle runs "on every work item", which for agents is hours. An item would expire before any person could give evidence, then be retired automatically. "Build cycle of its slice" is not defined. The board's draft says "reviewed after two cycles" without saying which kind. (2) "At most one new item starts per pilot": no pilot is running, so it is unclear whether any item may start. (3) Promotion needs the steward, who is not named. (4) The cap of three, the 30 days and the single renewal have no stated basis, and the board marks its own experiment limits as "not adopted". Because principle 5 makes EXPLORE the only way to try an addition, a mechanism that cannot run blocks all growth.
findings.suggestedFix: Define expiry in terms that fit the evidence: "30 days, or the decision after the first pilot that tests it, whichever comes first; an item that needs evidence from people does not expire for lack of a pilot, it is marked waiting". Say how many items may start while no pilot exists. Mark the three limits "[assumption] starting values from an unadopted board draft and the lead's judgment; reviewed at the first quarterly review".

findings.where: "ADAPT": "Inside these ranges, a product or an agent decides without asking." and "it goes to the human review queue"
findings.problem: (1) operating-model.md says a change inside an ADAPT range is decided by the lead after automated checks and a review one tier up. This file says the product or agent decides without asking. A builder cannot tell which applies. (2) An out-of-range value "goes to the human review queue", which will not be built until phase 4 and has no reviewers. Until then an out-of-range value has nowhere to go, and the queue has no rule for an item nobody votes on. (3) "After that, changing a range needs the CEO's agreement" implies the lead may change ranges freely between Gate 1 and Gate 2, although the charter is called load-bearing from Gate 1. (4) "Loosening one needs the CEO's agreement, because it is a change to a delta" uses "delta" to mean a limit; README.md defines it as a measured difference. (5) "These are the numeric budgets the constraints in CLAUDE.md ask for" points a newcomer at a file they have not seen.
findings.suggestedFix: State the two cases separately in both files: "A product choosing a value inside a range: no approval, recorded in its theme file. A change to the system's own default inside a range: the lead decides." Add: "Until the queue exists, an out-of-range value is pulled back to the reference. An item with no vote after 14 days is pulled back." Say who may change a range before Gate 2. Replace "a change to a delta" with "a change to a limit". Replace the CLAUDE.md sentence with "The CEO's brief asks for numeric performance budgets; these are they."

findings.where: "Subagents do not recruit subagents. Only the lead recruits. This keeps cost and responsibility visible in one place."
findings.problem: Strongest honest argument against. (1) Visibility of cost does not need a ban; a spending cap and a log give it. The ban makes one agent's attention the limit on all work: every split of a task and every review must pass through the lead. The 5-year vision has hundreds of surfaces, and principle 7 says maintenance cost must not rise with the number of products; the lead's coordination load does. The lead is also a single point of failure. (2) An Opus builder that discovers its task needs an independent check cannot get one without returning to the lead. (3) The CEO's notes asked this as an open question. The file answers it in one line with no alternative weighed, unlike the team model, which gets a table. (4) The stated benefit is an intention, not a measured result, and no condition is given for revisiting the rule.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep the rule as a starting rule and say so. Add the alternative considered (one level of delegation with a token cap and a log entry per recruit) and why it lost for now. Add a trigger: "Reviewed when work waits on the lead for briefs longer than a stated time, or at the first quarterly review." Change "This keeps" to "This is meant to keep".

findings.where: "No standing committee of agents." and the list of viewpoints beginning "a person using assistive technology"
findings.problem: Strongest honest argument against. (1) A fixed list of six viewpoints, recruited by the same lead with briefs the lead writes, is a standing panel in everything but memory. The file removes the one useful property of a committee, consistent judgment over time, and keeps the weakness it names: agents agreeing. Fresh reviewers do not know earlier rulings, so the same question can get different verdicts in different cycles. (2) Reviewers on the same model as the author share its blind spots; different prompts do not make them independent. (3) "A person using assistive technology" as a viewpoint played by an agent is role-play. Its verdict could be counted as accessibility evidence, which principle 1 and the board ("Test with people, not agent agreement") forbid. (4) For decisions no test can check, such as visual direction and voice, the result is that agents decide alone. The board asks for a human checkpoint there; this file has none.
findings.suggestedFix: Rename the first viewpoint "an accessibility specialist checking against published criteria" and add: "No agent viewpoint stands in for a person; its findings are never recorded as evidence about people." Require every reviewer brief to include the earlier decisions on the same question. Add one sentence admitting that same-model reviewers are not independent. Add a row to the decision table for visual direction and voice with the human checkpoint, marked waiting until a person is named.

findings.where: "Roles" ("Lead ... gate reviews"; "Reviewer: a fresh subagent one tier above the builder"), "Who decides what", and "The passport": "the person or agent who writes the first part never writes the third"
findings.problem: The file does not say how the lead's own work is checked. (1) No tier is above Fable, so "one tier above the builder" gives the lead no reviewer, and "moves up one tier" has nowhere to go. (2) The lead owns "gate reviews", including the gate on its own charter. (3) For a new component, a change inside ADAPT, or starting an EXPLORE item, the lead decides; when the lead also proposes, it writes parts one and three of the passport, which the passport forbids. For EXPLORE the lead is also the proof. (4) The lead writes the brief for its own reviewer, choosing the scope and what to look for, which weakens the word "independent". (5) No row covers changing or loosening a test or lint rule, although the build-cycle loop's action is to "change the ... lint rule that caused the failure". The lead can therefore weaken the instrument that measures it. The CEO's brief forbids this; the charter does not repeat it.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a role line: "The lead's own work is reviewed by a fresh agent on the same model. This is the weakest review in the system: same model, briefed by the author. It is recorded as such." Add rows: "A proposal by the lead: decided by the CEO or steward if it touches a LOCK item or a principle; otherwise by a reviewer whose verdict the lead may not overrule." and "Loosening or deleting a check: CEO only. Adding or tightening one: lead." Change "gate reviews" under Lead to "arranges gate reviews; does not judge its own work". Say what happens when Fable work fails review twice (it goes to the CEO's waiting list).

findings.where: "The four loops" (intro, table, and "A loop that corrects using old information overshoots")
findings.problem: Strongest honest argument against the claim that four loops at four speeds will correct the system. (1) By the table's own "Current state" row, one loop runs, "informally". The two loops that bring evidence from people and that revise the principles have no people. (2) The loops that can run compare the work with rules the same lead wrote. They can make the system agree with itself; they cannot show the rules are right for people. The strategy loop's sensor is mostly the pilot loop's evidence, so without pilots it reads only agent-made numbers. (3) The build-cycle sensor is three fixed tasks run by a model whose output varies from run to run. "Revert if it drops" with no repeat runs and no margin will revert good changes on noise, and tuning docs to three fixed tasks raises the score without improving the system. "First-pass review rate rises" can be met by easier briefs or kinder reviewers, and the lead controls both. (4) Signals pass outward to a loop that is not running: "a slice is ready for people" goes to a steward who does not exist, with no time limit. (5) The pilot loop has no cadence at all, so there are three speeds and one "when someone arranges it". The file's own argument about delay applies: agents may rebuild the system many times before the first evidence from a person arrives. (6) The intro says the file tells "how the system corrects itself" in the present tense. (7) The overshoot sentence is a general claim from the course notes summarised in notes/sources/2026-11-13-systems-notebook.md, stated as fact with no source or label. (8) "At or above the baseline" has no baseline to refer to: there is no existing checkout to measure.
findings.suggestedFix: Change the intro to "how the system is meant to correct itself; one of four loops runs today". Add a row "What this loop cannot tell us". For the benchmark state the number of runs per score and the margin that counts as a drop. Add to the build-cycle desired state a counter-measure that cannot be gamed the same way (for example, defects found later in work that passed first time). Give the pilot loop a minimum cadence once a steward exists, and say what the lead does while it is absent (nothing ships to people; the charter stays provisional). Cite the notebook for the overshoot sentence and label it [pattern]. Point to checkout-slice.md for what the baseline is.

findings.where: "Team model": "He later wrote that a federated model rarely succeeds without a central team."
findings.problem: The survey reviewer corrected exactly this wording. notes/survey/thinkers.md says "rare" understated the source: Curtis reports no case of federated-only success among more than 80 systems without investment in central capacity. The notes also say his original pages would not open and the three models were read from a mirror.
findings.suggestedFix: Write: "He later wrote that, across more than 80 systems, he had seen no federated model succeed without investment in a central team (read from his Substack; the three models were read from a mirror of his 2015 article)."

findings.where: "The human review queue"; "Retiring"; loops table "Running informally from this commit"; "Where things are said"
findings.problem: (1) The queue has no number of votes, no rule for a tie and no rule for silence; one like from one colleague starts a proposal to widen a range. (2) The retirement rule for a skill ("fewer than half ... across three uses") rests on three uses, which is too few to tell a bad skill from bad luck, and the threshold has no stated basis. (3) "From this commit" means nothing to a reader of the file. (4) "The daily five-line digest" and "sandbox channel" appear with no explanation.
findings.suggestedFix: State a minimum number of votes and reviewers, and that an item with no votes after a set time is pulled back. Mark the skill threshold "[assumption] starting value". Replace "from this commit" with the date. Add one sentence saying what the digest is and who it is for.

strongestCounterargument: The charter is a closed loop with no person in it, and approving it as load-bearing hides that. An agent wrote the seven promises, the LOCK list and about twenty numbers. Agents will build to them, agents will check the building, an agent on the same model reviews the gate, and the benchmark measures whether a weaker agent can follow the docs. Every sensor that can run today measures agreement with the charter. None measures whether the charter is right for the people the first three principles are owed to. The sensors that could (the pilot loop, the strategy loop, the review queue, the steward) are all defined and all empty, and the CEO has said people come later. So the system can reach "zero drift" and a rising benchmark while being wrong, and it would look healthy on its own scorecard. Meanwhile the change rules make the content harder to alter than it was to create: an agent's gate verdict turns the LOCK list into brick, after which only a person may change it. A more honest alternative is to make brick only what is anchored outside the system (WCAG 2.2 level AA, showing the full price before commitment, the token rules the CEO's brief sets) and to keep everything the lead chose itself as dated clay with an expiry: the added human-agency principle, the order of principles 4 to 7, every ADAPT range, the EXPLORE limits, and the byte budgets. Each would be promoted only when a person has read it or a measurement supports it. If the charter is approved as drafted, the decision log should record that no person approved the LOCK list, that only one of the four loops runs, and that every number set by the lead is a starting guess.

lens: Checkability and falsifiability: can each contract, LOCK row, ADAPT range, EXPLORE limit, performance budget, decision-table row and loop sensor actually be checked, and can it fail. Reviewed all sections of README.md, vision.md, principles.md, budget.md and operating-model.md, against the Gate 1 pass criteria written in PROGRESS.md. Verdict note: the structure is sound and no redesign is needed, but four items would fail the written gate criteria as the text stands (criteria 1, 2, 3 and 10), so the drafts cannot become brick until those are closed. Every blocker is an edit to existing text. No file is clean under this lens.

findings.where: "How the ranking works": "They do not trade against each other. If two of them appear to conflict, work stops and the steward decides."
findings.problem: Gate criterion 2 says the ranking settles every conflict between two principles. For principles 1 to 3 the ranking settles nothing: it hands the conflict to a steward who is not named, whose seat is held by a CEO who has said they are not watching. "Work stops" also contradicts the hands-off rule in CLAUDE.md (choose the most reversible option, record it, continue). Conflicts inside this group are not hypothetical. Example: principle 3 says what a person entered is kept when something goes wrong, while the Safe behaviour LOCK row says payment details are never kept longer than the task needs; a failed card payment puts the card security code under both.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace the sentence with a rule that works with no human present: "If two of principles 1 to 3 conflict, the option that satisfies both is found or neither option ships. The item is marked blocked, the conflict is logged under Awaiting CEO in DECISIONS.md with both options, and other work continues. The steward's later ruling is added to this file as a worked case." Then record the conflicts already visible (the card security code case; a default delivery option versus "no choice made in advance that costs money") with a ruling or an explicit "awaiting steward" entry. Alternatively rank 1, 2, 3 strictly and say so.

findings.where: Principle 5 rule, "The performance budgets are part of this rule" and "Class. ADAPT"; principle 1 rule, "on a slow connection and on a low-end phone"
findings.problem: The performance budgets have three incompatible statuses. Principle 5 (fifth in rank, class ADAPT) owns them.
