Principle 1 (LOCK) also claims performance through "slow connection" and "low-end phone". budget.md enforces them as hard checks that fail a change and can only be loosened by the CEO. So the ranking rule does not settle a real conflict: when principle 1 or 4 needs more bytes (three required themes, including increased-contrast, inside 12 kilobytes), the ranking says the higher principle wins and the check says the change fails. A builder cannot tell whether a budget breach blocks release.
findings.suggestedFix: Give the budgets one status in both files: "Performance budgets are hard checks in L1. They are not traded by rank. If meeting a LOCK row is impossible inside a budget, the change is blocked and the budget goes to the CEO under Awaiting CEO." In principle 1, replace "on a slow connection and on a low-end phone" with a pointer to the named budgets and test profile in budget.md, so the clause has evidence.

findings.where: Principle 4 rule, "A new pattern goes into the system, never into product code"; principle 5 rule, "Something is added only when ... the need has appeared more than once"; principle 5 class, "EXPLORE as the only way to try an addition"
findings.problem: Together these leave no legal home for the first occurrence of a new need. It may not live in product code (principle 4). It may not enter the system until the need has appeared twice (principle 5). EXPLORE is clay, and README says clay is never shipped. The ranking formally lets principle 4 win, which makes the "more than once" clause dead text. There are also two contradicting routes for an addition: principle 5 says EXPLORE is the only way, while operating-model.md row 3 lets the lead approve a new component or token directly. And budget.md allows one new EXPLORE item per pilot while no pilot is running, so the only route is closed today.
findings.suggestedFix: Write the single route in principle 5 and mirror it in the decision table: "A first occurrence is built as an EXPLORE item, in a marked folder, counted on the scorecard. It may be shown in a pilot but not released. A second independent occurrence, recorded in a passport, makes it eligible to enter the system." State that the four checkout parts are the founding set and exempt. Delete or reword decision-table row 3 so it covers changes to existing parts only, and fix the "one per pilot" limit as described in the EXPLORE finding.

findings.where: Principle 1: rule, evidence and trigger
findings.problem: Three terms in the rule decide whether a screen breaks it and none is defined: "core task", "slow connection", "low-end phone". The last two have no evidence at all. No list of supported browsers and assistive technologies exists anywhere in the charter, so "with a screen reader" cannot be tested the same way twice. The L3 evidence promises that people who use a keyboard, a screen reader or magnification take part in every pilot, but the operating model does not commit to recruiting them. The trigger ("any barrier that stops a person completing a task") is narrower than the rule: a WCAG AA failure that does not stop completion breaks the rule but does not fire the trigger. Nothing senses a barrier found after release, because L3 covers pilots only.
findings.suggestedFix: Define "core task" in README as the named task list of each slice (for checkout: reach the page, enter details, see the total, pay, see the result). Replace the two device clauses with a pointer to the test profile in budget.md. Add a support list (browsers and versions, screen reader and browser pairs) or name the file that will hold it and the gate that confirms it. Change the trigger to "any failed LOCK accessibility check, or any barrier seen in a session or reported by a user". Add to the pilot definition in operating-model.md that each pilot includes at least one keyboard-only and one screen reader participant, or that the component status stays "automated checks only".

findings.where: Principle 2 rule: "no choice made for the person in advance that costs them money or shares their data" and "Content produced by a machine, or that may be wrong, says so"
findings.problem: Two reviewers would not agree on the first slice. A checkout must show some delivery method; a preselected standard delivery at a price is, read literally, a choice made in advance that costs money, so the rule bans a normal default. "Or that may be wrong" has no boundary: a delivery date estimate, an estimated tax line and a stock count may all be wrong. "Implies" has no test.
findings.suggestedFix: Scope the first clause: "No optional extra that adds cost or shares data is selected in advance. Where the person must pick one of several priced options, the cheapest is selected and its price is in the total." Bound the second: "Content is marked when it is an estimate, a prediction, or text generated by a model", and name the three kinds in the component contract as a required source field (measured, estimated, generated). For "implies", point to the list of banned patterns in voice-and-tone.md so the writing check has something to match.

findings.where: Principle 3 rule: "An action that cannot be undone, spends money or shares data asks first and shows what will happen"; evidence: "a destructive action is never the default"
findings.problem: "Asks first" does not say whether the pay button is itself the ask or whether a separate confirmation step must follow it. One reading adds a confirmation dialog to every payment, which principle 3 would then force over principle 5. The matching LOCK row in budget.md lists only "cannot be undone" and "spends money" and drops "shares data", so the two files state different rules. "Default" is not defined (first focus, the action Enter triggers, the visually primary button, or a preselected option), so the markup lint named in budget.md has nothing precise to check. The clauses "the way to reverse it is offered" and "does not commit on the person's behalf" have no evidence.
findings.suggestedFix: Define it: "The control that commits states the consequence in its own label or directly beside it (for payment, the amount). A separate confirmation step is required only when the action cannot be undone and the consequence is not visible at the control." Make the budget.md row use the same three cases. Define default as "the control that receives first focus, the control Enter activates, or the visually primary control". Add evidence for reversal (a component test that an undo control is present for each reversible action in the contract) or mark it as review-only.

findings.where: Principle 4 rule: "Things that mean the same look and behave the same" and "Appearance may vary inside the ranges"; "Class. Meaning and behaviour are LOCK. Appearance is ADAPT."
findings.problem: The rule contradicts itself in one paragraph: the same thing must look the same, and appearance may vary. A reviewer cannot say whether a button with a different corner radius in a second product breaks it. "Pattern" is not defined, so "a new pattern goes into the system" cannot be applied. The class line also contradicts "How the ranking works", which says principles 1 to 3 are the LOCK items and 4 to 7 trade by rank: part of principle 4 is LOCK, so it is unclear who rules when it meets a principle from the first group (the ranking, which the lead applies, or a LOCK change, which is the steward's).
findings.suggestedFix: Reword: "Inside one product, things that mean the same look and behave the same. Across products, meaning and behaviour are identical and appearance may differ only inside the ADAPT ranges." Define pattern in README (for example: a reusable arrangement of components that solves a named task). In "How the ranking works", add: "The Meaning rows of principle 4 are also LOCK. Rank decides which principle shapes a design; it never permits shipping a LOCK breach."

findings.where: "Class. ADAPT" on principles 5, 6 and 7
findings.problem: README defines ADAPT as a delta allowed inside a written range. budget.md has no reference and no range for anything in principles 5, 6 or 7 (counts of parts, dependencies, domain separation). Several of their clauses are zero-tolerance rules enforced by lint, which is LOCK behaviour under an ADAPT label: "Nothing in brick depends on software its maker calls beta", "nothing in the core mentions a domain", "Every breaking change comes with a version, a notice and a way to migrate". A builder cannot tell what a breach of these costs.
findings.suggestedFix: Either remove the class line from 5 to 7 and say "enforced by the L1 and L2 checks named above; not a delta class", or add rows to budget.md that give each a reference and range (for example: count of button variants, reference 3, range 2 to 4). For the zero-tolerance clauses say plainly: "this check blocks a merge".

findings.where: Principle 5: rule, evidence and trigger
findings.problem: "Distinct need" and "appeared more than once" have no counting rule (two screens, two flows or two products). The evidence lists counts of components, variants and tokens and the shipped size, but scorecard.md has none of these measures and the L2 sensor (review and benchmark) cannot produce them. The trigger "a variant unused for two releases" needs usage data that does not exist until the telemetry planned in item 4.2; with no consuming products every variant is unused, so the trigger either never fires or fires on everything. "Each release may remove things" cannot be broken.
findings.suggestedFix: Define an occurrence as a use in a separate flow, recorded in a passport. Name an inventory script that counts components, variants and tokens from the source on every cycle, and propose the three counts and compressed size as scorecard measures under Awaiting CEO (scorecard definitions are the CEO's). Define "unused" as zero references in the reference pages and in registered product repositories, and report "not measured" until the nightly scan exists. Replace "may remove" with the checkable line already in vision.md: at least one release per quarter removes more than it adds, with the unit stated.

findings.where: Principle 6: rule, evidence and trigger
findings.problem: "Nothing is styled after a trend" cannot be checked and has no evidence or trigger; by this file's own retirement test (no check exists and none can be built) it should go. "A web standard before a library" has no support threshold, so a standard that few browsers ship would satisfy it. "Software its maker calls beta" has no detection rule. "Breaking change" is not defined and the count is self-reported. "What replacing it would cost" has no unit. The trigger "a contract that only works in one framework" has no sensor, because only one implementation will exist.
findings.suggestedFix: Delete the trend sentence or move it to visual direction as taste guidance. Add a support threshold for web platform features (for example, shipped in the current and previous major version of each browser on the support list). Detect beta by a script that fails on any brick dependency with a pre-release version tag or a version below 1.0, with a written exception list. Define the public surface (token names, component names, class and attribute names, contract fields) and a script that diffs it between releases; any removal or rename is a breaking change. Define replacement cost as the count of files outside one adapter folder that import the dependency. Make the contract tests run against rendered HTML only, so they are framework-free by construction.

findings.where: Principle 7: "The cost of maintaining the system must not rise in step with the number of products" and its evidence
findings.problem: Nothing measures this clause. "Cost per component" on the scorecard is the cost to build one component once, not the cost of maintenance as products are added, and with one product there is no trend to read. The benchmark is listed as evidence, but three ecommerce tasks cannot show that the core is free of commerce (DECISIONS.md A-05 says as much). "A domain word in the core" needs a word list before a lint can run. The import lint is an L1 check but is listed under L2.
findings.suggestedFix: Define maintenance cost as tokens and human hours spent on system changes per release, divided by the number of consuming products, reported as "not measured" until two products exist; propose it as a scorecard measure under Awaiting CEO. State which benchmark number counts against principle 7 (for example, violations that add a one-off part), or remove the benchmark from this principle's evidence until the booking task exists. Name the domain word list as a section of the vocabulary file and move the import lint to L1.

findings.where: "What makes a principle useful, and when one is retired": "it decided nothing in the quarter"
findings.problem: This test would rewrite or retire a LOCK principle after a quiet quarter. A floor that nobody contested is working, not useless. "Decided a real disagreement" also has no observable form: one lead agent decides almost everything, so there is rarely a second party, and the lead can tag any decision with a principle to keep it alive. The same weakness is in vision.md ("Did the vision decide at least one real disagreement this quarter?") and in the L4 desired state. The L4 sensor does not list the decision log, which is the only place this could be read from.
findings.suggestedFix: Exempt principles 1 to 3 from this test. Define "decided" as any of: a DECISIONS.md or passport entry that records at least two options and cites the principle as the reason; a reviewer finding upheld by citing it; or its check failing at least once in the quarter. Add DECISIONS.md and the passports to the L4 sensor in operating-model.md.

findings.where: Evidence lines: principle 2 "In our own work", principle 4 "Nightly", principle 6 "Every release", principle 7 "When a second domain is built"
findings.problem: The file says each evidence item names the loop that collects it. These four name no loop, and "nightly" and "every release" are not cadences of any loop in operating-model.md. L1 to L4 are used here before they are defined.
findings.suggestedFix: Assign each to a loop (nightly scan and per-release counts to L2 with the lead as owner; label and source checks to the L2 review checklist) and add one line near the top: "L1 to L4 are the four loops defined in operating-model.md: every change, every work item, every pilot, every quarter."

findings.where: Principle 2 claims: "Unexpected extra costs are a leading reason ... the method and sample are not public"
findings.problem: The wording goes past the reviewed source in notes/survey/checkout-evidence.md. The source item is "extra costs too high", not "unexpected". The note records that the 40% and 12% exclude the 42% of shoppers who were only browsing, which changes how the figures read, and that no sample size is given while the page describes its method in two ways; "the method and sample are not public" says something different. Principle 2 binds our own reports.
findings.suggestedFix: Reword to: "Extra costs are the reason most often given for abandoning a purchase [research]: Baymard Institute's list, shown as updated 28 October 2026, reports 40% for 'extra costs too high' and 12% for not being able to see the total up front, among shoppers who were not just browsing. The page gives no sample size." Link the note file.

findings.where: LOCK tables, rows: "No invented urgency, scarcity or social pressure"; "Content produced by a machine, or that may be wrong, is marked as such"; "A status shows the real state"; "The full price, including every charge"; "Each token is used only for its stated purpose"; "Payment details ... never kept in the page longer than the task needs"
findings.problem: Gate criterion 3 asks that every LOCK item name the check that detects a breach. For these six rows the named check cannot detect the breach. A writing check sees words, not whether stock or a deadline is real. A checklist or lint cannot know where content came from unless the source is declared. A component test proves each state renders, not that the product passed the true state or every charge. A token-usage lint cannot recognise "decoration" unless each token declares where it may be used. "Longer than the task needs" has no measurable limit, and "no component stores them" is a claim, not a check. A LOCK row that cannot be detected is a promise the system cannot show it keeps.
findings.suggestedFix: Give each row a declared fact that a check can read. Urgency: any quantity, deadline or popularity text must come from a named data field in the component contract; lint fails on such words in literal strings. Machine content: a required source field (measured, estimated, generated) and a component test that the marker renders for the last two. Real state: the status part takes a state from a defined set driven by the request result, plus a flow test on the reference checkout with a delayed and a failing network stub that asserts "saved" never shows before success. Full price: a flow test asserting the amount sent to the payment stub equals the total shown before the commit control was pressed. Token purpose: each semantic token lists allowed CSS properties and allowed components; lint enforces the list. Payment details: lint that bans writes to storage, cookies and URLs in components, and a flow test that no card value remains in the page after the result screen. For anything still not detectable, label the row "review only, not machine-checked" so the status is true.

findings.where: LOCK tables, rows whose check is a review checklist, a screenshot or a "visual test": colour alone; re-entering information; options selected in advance; confirmation before an irreversible or paid action; focus visible; reflow at 320 pixels and 200% text; name, role, state and value
findings.problem: An automated check is feasible for each and the row either names a checklist or names a check too loosely to fail. A visual test compares with a stored picture, so a baseline that already scrolls sideways passes forever. "With screenshots" does not say what is asserted. A greyscale picture needs a judge. Markup lint cannot tell which preselected option costs money without a declaration. The confirmation row cites a component test, but none of the four parts is a confirmation component. The "named manual check" has no person to do it today.
findings.suggestedFix: Reflow: assert the page's scroll width does not exceed 320 pixels and no text is clipped, at root text size 200%. Focus: assert a focus indicator of stated minimum thickness and contrast, and that the focused element is not covered (hit-test its centre), including under the sticky pay bar on the reference page. Colour alone: for each pair of states in the contract, assert a difference in text, icon or attribute, not only in colour. Re-entry: a flow test that induces an error and goes back and forward, asserting fields keep their values. Preselection: lint flags every input selected in advance unless the contract declares it has no cost or data effect. Confirmation: a flow test on the reference checkout that the commit control's accessible name includes the amount. Name, role, state: assertions on the browser's accessibility tree against the contract. Where a manual check stays, say who does it and that the status reads "not done" until a person has.

findings.where: Accessibility table, rows 1 and 2: "Contrast check on every declared text and background token pair" and "Contrast check on declared pairs"
findings.problem: The check only sees pairs someone declared. A component that puts a text token on a background nobody declared is a real breach the check will never report. The row also does not say how the check knows which pairs carry large text, whether disabled states are exempt (WCAG exempts them; "their states" here does not), or that it runs on a product's own theme, which matters because the ADAPT table allows any accent hue.
findings.suggestedFix: Add two checks: a lint that fails when a component uses a text and background combination that is not in the declared list, and a rendered contrast scan of every component state in every theme. State the disabled-state exemption or its absence. Each declared pair carries its text size class. Ship the contrast check as a command a product runs on its own theme file, and make passing it the condition in the ADAPT colour rows.

findings.where: "Accessibility (WCAG 2.2 level AA is the floor)" table as a whole
findings.problem: The heading makes all of WCAG 2.2 level AA a LOCK, but the table names checks for eleven requirements. Criteria that bear directly on the checkout slice have no row and no check, for example status messages announced to assistive technology (4.1.3, the feedback part), input purpose identified (1.3.5, the field part), text spacing (1.4.12), adjustable time limits (2.2.1, payment sessions) and accessible authentication (3.3.8). A builder would read the table as the complete list.
findings.suggestedFix: Say that the table is a summary and name a file, to be completed in phase 3 and confirmed at Gate 3, that lists every level A and AA success criterion with one of: automated check (named), manual check (named, with who does it), or not applicable (with the reason). Add rows now for 4.1.3 and 1.3.5 because the four parts depend on them.

findings.where: Performance budgets: "JavaScript needed to read the page and complete the core task | None", against Safe behaviour rows "A second press of a submit control does not submit twice" and "Valid input survives an error", and Truthful content row "A status shows the real state: loading, saved, failed, sent"
findings.problem: These are not mutually consistent as written. With no JavaScript, a button cannot ignore a second press, a loading state cannot be shown, and input survives an error only if the server sends it back. The system is a front-end system and does not own the server. Either the LOCK rows are unmet in the no-JavaScript case or the budget is.
findings.suggestedFix: State how each LOCK row is met without JavaScript: the component contract includes a server side (a hidden one-time submission key the server must honour, and server-rendered error markup that carries the entered values and the error text), and the reference checkout implements it so a test with JavaScript turned off can assert all three. Or state that these rows are met by the enhancement layer and that the no-JavaScript path guarantees only a named subset. Add the test "core task completes with JavaScript disabled" as the check for the budget row.

findings.where: Rows "A person is never asked to re-enter information they already gave in the same task", "Valid input survives an error" and "Payment details and other sensitive values are never kept in the page longer than the task needs"
findings.problem: Two LOCK rows demand that input is kept and a third demands that sensitive input is dropped. After a failed card payment the card security code falls under all three, and payment fields hosted by a payment provider usually clear on error. A LOCK delta must be zero, so one row is breached whatever is built. "Never" is also stricter than WCAG 2.2 criterion 3.3.7, which allows re-entry for security.
findings.suggestedFix: Add the exception to both rows: "except values that must be re-entered for security, which are listed in the component contract (for example the card security code)". Then the flow test can assert that every field not on that list keeps its value.

findings.where: ADAPT table, row "Reading measure | 60 characters | 45 to 75 characters per line", with "What must still hold: Reflow at 320 pixels" and the 16 pixel text floor
findings.problem: The lower end of the range cannot be met on the mobile-first slice. At 320 pixels wide with body text at 16 pixels or more, a line holds roughly 35 to 40 characters before any side padding (an estimate that assumes an average character is about half the text size wide), and fewer at 200% text. Every small-screen page would be reported as outside its range and sent to the human review queue.
findings.suggestedFix: State the range as a ceiling with a conditional floor: "at most 75 characters per line; at least 45 only where the container is wide enough to hold 45 at the current text size". Give the script the rule in those terms.

findings.where: ADAPT table, rows Colour theme, Accent and neutral colours, Typeface, Density, Motion
findings.problem: A script could not evaluate these ranges. Increased-contrast is required but has no threshold, so a copy of the light theme would pass. "Any hue" names no colour space and does not say lightness and saturation steps are kept; it also lets a product pick an accent in the danger hue, which principle 4 gives as a breach. Typeface says "Line height and measure stay in range" but no line-height range is written anywhere. Density gives both "three named steps" and a continuous "0.75 to 1.25", and its floor depends on "touch screens" and "primary controls", neither defined. Motion says a product "may shorten" durations and also that transitions "run for 0 to 500 milliseconds", which disagree on whether lengthening is allowed.
findings.suggestedFix: Increased-contrast: state a ratio (for example 7 to 1 for text) or define it relative to the default theme. Accent: "hue may change; the lightness and chroma of each scale step are fixed, in a named colour space; the accent hue stays at least a stated distance from each status hue". Typeface: write the line-height range. Density: choose either three fixed multipliers or a continuous range; define touch by the browser's coarse-pointer signal and name which controls count as primary in the component contract. Motion: one rule, either "at most the reference duration" or "0 to 500 milliseconds".

findings.where: "EXPLORE: outside the range, for a limited time": expiry and limits
findings.problem: The limits are not enforceable as written. No register of EXPLORE items is named, so nothing can count to three, read an expiry date or see a second renewal. The expiry "the end of the second build cycle of its slice, whichever comes first" is hours at agent speed, because a build cycle runs on every work item; an item would expire before any evidence from people could exist. "At most one new item starts per pilot" is undefined while no pilot runs: it means either none or unlimited. "Renewed once" and "revised once" look like two rules for one thing. "Retired automatically" names no actor. The operating model puts an item into the human queue at its expiry, the same moment it is retired automatically, and the lead reads votes weekly, so a vote can never arrive in time.
findings.suggestedFix: Name a register file with one entry per item (owner, hypothesis, start, expiry, evidence, renewals) and an L1 check that fails when more than three are active, when an entry is incomplete, or when brick imports an item. Tie expiry to the calendar only (30 days), or to the end of the pilot that tests it. Replace "per pilot" with a calendar limit until pilots run. Use one word for the single extension and say whether it restarts the clock. Make the nightly scan open the removal change for an expired item. Put an item in the queue a stated number of days before expiry.

findings.where: "Performance budgets": the measurement sentence and the rows for largest contentful paint, interaction to next paint and compressed sizes
findings.problem: The budgets are not measurable as stated. "A simulated mid-range phone on a slow 4G connection" gives no processor slowdown, bandwidth, delay, tool, version or number of runs, so two runs can disagree about 2.5 seconds and a single run will make the check fail at random. Interaction to next paint needs interactions; a page-load lab run has none, so the row needs a scripted set of interactions or a different lab measure. "Compressed" names no algorithm or level. It is not said whether the 12 kilobytes covers all three required themes, or whether fonts count in the 100 kilobytes. Principle 1 says "low-end phone" and this file says "mid-range". The L1 sensor in operating-model.md lists payload size only, so the three timing budgets have no sensor.
findings.suggestedFix: Write the profile as numbers (processor slowdown factor, download and upload speed, round-trip delay), the tool and its version, and "median of five runs". For interaction to next paint, name the scripted interactions (type in a field, trigger an error, press pay) and measure across them, or replace the row with total blocking time for the load. State the compression algorithm and level. State which themes the CSS budget includes and that fonts count toward total transfer. Use one device word in both files. Add the timing run to the L1 sensor list.

findings.where: "What 'zero drift' means", counts 1 and 2
findings.problem: Neither count can be trusted to reach a true zero. Count 1 needs a written list of values that are not drift (zero, percentages, keywords such as inherit, and breakpoint widths, which cannot be read from a CSS custom property inside a media query); without it the lint either never reaches zero or hides exceptions. Count 2 depends on a scan that must recognise a second implementation; a scan can catch obvious cases (a component with a system name that is not imported from the system, a native button with its own styling) but not a look-alike under another name, so its zero means "none found", not "none exist". Product code lives outside this repository and nothing says how it is scanned.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish the allow-list and say how breakpoints are tokenised (substituted at build time). List the scan's detection rules, test the scan against planted duplicates on every cycle, and report the count as "none detected by rules 1 to N" with the share of planted duplicates it caught. State the scope: this repository's reference pages now; product repositories once they register and run the same command.

findings.where: ADAPT intro: "it goes to the human review queue ... and it is either pulled back, or becomes an EXPLORE item"; closing note on 44 pixels, 16 pixels and 45 to 75 characters
findings.problem: The outcome for an out-of-range value differs from operating-model.md, which says a liked item becomes a proposal to widen the range or to promote. The closing note calls the three numbers inferred from patterns but does not use the [pattern] label or cite the survey files.
findings.suggestedFix: Use one sentence in both files for the outcomes (pulled back; EXPLORE item; proposal to widen the range, which is the CEO's decision). Tag the note [pattern] and link the notes/survey files it rests on.

findings.where: "The passport": "the person or agent who writes the first part never writes the third"; "Who decides what" rows 2, 3 and 5; Roles: "Reviewer | A fresh subagent one tier above the builder"; "Escalation"
findings.problem: Every row has a decider, but for the commonest case today the decider is barred. The file says the core is the only contributor, so the lead proposes most changes, and rows 2, 3 and 5 make the lead the decider, which the passport forbids. No tier exists above the lead, so "a reviewer one tier up" cannot be supplied for the lead's own work, and "fails review twice moves up one tier" has nowhere to go at the top tier. CLAUDE.md covers the review half (a fresh-context reviewer at the same tier) but this file does not, and neither says who decides.
findings.suggestedFix: Add to the table notes: "When the lead is the proposer, proof is written by a fresh-context reviewer at the lead's tier, and the decision is the reviewer's verdict; the lead may not overrule it and may only escalate to the CEO under Awaiting CEO." Add to Escalation: "Work at the top tier that fails review twice is marked blocked and reported to the CEO." Update the Reviewer role to say "one tier above the builder, or a fresh context at the same tier for the lead".

findings.where: "Who decides what" table: missing kinds of change
findings.problem: Several kinds of change have no row. (1) Loosening, disabling or deleting a check or lint rule: a LOCK row can be emptied by weakening its check while the row stays untouched. (2) Tightening or loosening a performance budget (stated in budget.md, absent here). (3) Changing parts of the charter the last row does not list: the vision, the roles, the loops and this table itself, so the lead could change its own decision rights. (4) Passing a gate, which is what turns clay into brick. (5) Renewing, revising or retiring an EXPLORE item at expiry. (6) Rolling back a release when a LOCK breach is found: only the steward may, and the steward seat is held by an absent CEO. (7) Adding or replacing a dependency. (8) Changing a component's accessibility status from "automated checks only".
findings.suggestedFix: Add rows. Loosening or removing a check: never to make a change pass; for a check behind a LOCK row the steward decides, otherwise the CEO. Budgets: lead tightens, CEO loosens. Charter text outside the last row: lead proposes, fresh-context reviewer proves, CEO decides for roles and decision rights. Gate pass: the gate reviewer decides, the lead cannot. EXPLORE at expiry: lead for renew and retire, steward for promote. Rollback after a LOCK breach: anyone may roll back to the last good release at once and must log it; only the steward may release again. Dependency: lead, with the replacement-cost record. Accessibility status: steward, on session evidence.

findings.where: "Who decides what", row "A change inside an ADAPT range | ... | Lead"
findings.problem: budget.md says "Inside these ranges, a product or an agent decides without asking." This row says the lead decides after automated checks and a reviewer one tier up. A builder working on a product theme cannot tell which applies.
findings.suggestedFix: Split the row. "A product using a value inside an ADAPT range: decided by the product or its agent; proof is the automated range check and the entry in the theme file; rolled back by the product." "A change to the system's own default inside an ADAPT range: decided by the lead after checks and review."

findings.where: "The four loops" table, column L2: Variable, Desired state, Sensor, Actuator
findings.problem: The L2 sensor cannot produce the L2 variable. The variable is the scorecard and the benchmark; the sensor is "review one tier up; the benchmark". Review yields only the first-pass rate. The other scorecard measures come from sources no loop lists: the nightly scan (raw values, duplicates), tool usage reports (cost), the queue export, and the counts and dependency list that principles 5 and 6 cite. The benchmark cannot return a number until published docs exist in phase 4, yet the current state reads "running informally". The actuator keeps a change "if the benchmark holds, revert if it drops", but a benchmark run by a model varies from run to run and reports three numbers (completion, violations, tool calls); without repeated runs and a stated margin the loop will revert good changes and keep bad ones on noise. "First-pass review rate rises" is a direction, not a state a loop can reach. The nightly scan, the per-release counts and the weekly reading of the queue have no loop and no owner.
findings.suggestedFix: List every sensor that feeds the scorecard, with its cadence and owner, and attach the nightly scan and the release counts to L2 under the lead. State the current state truthfully: "review running; benchmark not running until docs are published". Define the comparison: a fixed number of benchmark runs before and after, a stated order of the three numbers (for example violations, then completion, then tool calls), and the size of difference that counts as a drop. Replace "rises" with a target band, set after a baseline exists.

findings.where: "The human review queue"
findings.problem: The queue is the only stated destination for a value outside its range and it cannot act. It has no reviewers and is not built until phase 4, and no default is given for the time before that or for an item nobody votes on. "A liked item" has no threshold: one like, a majority, or a minimum number of votes. Nothing says who may be a reviewer.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a default: "Until the queue has reviewers, and for any item with no vote after a stated number of days, the item is treated as disliked and pulled back to the reference." State the rule for liked (for example at least three votes and a majority). Say who names reviewers (the steward) and that the item stays out of brick while it waits.

findings.where: L3 column: "Desired state: Task success and understanding at or above the baseline" and "Actuator: Approve, revise or retire"; "Retiring" paragraph
findings.problem: L3 has no rule that maps a pilot result to approve, revise or retire, and no start condition beyond "no steward, no participants". The retirement rule for a brief template or skill needs a record of which template or skill each piece of work used; nothing collects that.
findings.suggestedFix: Point L3 to the section of checkout-slice.md or the pilot plan that states the decision rule and the minimum number of sessions, or say it is not yet written and which item writes it. Add "brief template or skill used" to the record kept for each work item in PROGRESS.md.

findings.where: "Team model": "He later wrote that a federated model rarely succeeds without a central team."
findings.problem: The reviewed note in notes/survey/thinkers.md records that "rare" understated the source: Curtis reports no case of federated-only success among more than 80 systems without investment in a central team. The charter repeats the wording the reviewer corrected.
findings.suggestedFix: Change to: "He later wrote that, across more than 80 systems, he had seen no federated model succeed without investment in a central team."

findings.where: Whole file, against Gate 1 criterion 1 in PROGRESS.md: "It fits on one screen."
findings.problem: The file is 76 lines and 877 words. It does not fit on one screen under any ordinary reading, and the criterion itself gives no size, so the gate reviewer has to guess.
findings.suggestedFix: Either cut the file to the north star, the four horizons with their checks, and the usefulness test (moving "Why this is needed now" and "What the system is not" to README or a short second file), or record in DECISIONS.md what "one screen" means in lines or words and meet that number.

findings.where: "Where the system should be" and "Why this is needed now"
findings.problem: Several horizon checks cannot fail as written. The horizons have no dates, so nothing can be late. "One release has removed more than it added" names no unit. The one-year headline, "costs no more to maintain than it did with one", has no check beneath it. "The seven principles are still recognisable" cannot be judged and conflicts with principles.md, which expects principles to be merged or retired. "A difference that nobody decided on used to appear a few times a quarter" is a statement of a past rate with no label; the next sentence says it is not measured, so by principle 2 the figure should not be stated.
findings.suggestedFix: Anchor each horizon to a date counted from the Gate 1 pass. Give the unit for removal (components, variants and tokens counted together). Add a one-year check: maintenance cost per release with three products is no higher than with one, using the measure proposed for principle 7. Replace "still recognisable" with "every change to the principles since Gate 1 has a decision entry that cites evidence". Rewrite the rate sentence without a frequency and tag it [assumption].

findings.where: "Terms used in the charter"
findings.problem: Gate criterion 10 requires every special term to be defined where it first appears or in this file. These are used in the four files and defined in neither place: pilot; scorecard; baseline; cycle and build cycle; L1 to L4 (used in principles.md, which is read before operating-model.md); primitive, semantic and component token; core task; writing check; vocabulary file; theme file; component status; reference checkout page; design source; nightly scan; approvals list; phase and Gate 2; core and domain layer; "the board", "the brief" and "Rams"; CLAUDE.md and DECISIONS.md. "Contract" is defined only as a principle's contract, but budget.md and principle 6 use it for a component's contract, which is the reference every behaviour delta is measured against. One word with two meanings breaks principle 4 inside the charter.
findings.suggestedFix: Add one line per term. Use two distinct names for the two kinds of contract (for example "principle contract" and "component contract") and say what a component contract contains (markup, states, behaviour, accessible name, tokens used). Say in one line each what the board, the brief, CLAUDE.md and DECISIONS.md are, for a reader who has seen none of the work.

findings.where: "Read in this order", item 7 "benchmark.md"; term "Drift"
findings.problem: At the time of this review charter/benchmark.md does not exist in the folder (the other linked files do), so the link may be dead at the gate. The definition of drift ("a difference ... that nobody decided on") does not match budget.md, whose three counts include every raw value and every second implementation whether or not someone decided on it.
findings.suggestedFix: Confirm the benchmark file exists before the gate, or point item 7 at the section of checkout-slice.md that holds the three tasks. Align the two drift definitions: either the counts exclude recorded EXPLORE items, or the README definition drops "that nobody decided on".

strongestCounterargument: The charter's central claim is that every promise is a contract a check can fail, but today not one check exists, and no check has been shown to catch the breach it is named for. A named check is not a check. The same agent wrote the rules, will write the checks, will run them and will read the results, and a fresh-context reviewer on the same model shares its blind spots. The only loop that produces evidence about people (L3) has no steward, no participants and no start condition, so the three LOCK principles can at present fail only where an automated scan happens to look, which budget.md itself says is a part of the problems that exist. The contract form therefore gives an appearance of verifiability that is larger than what can actually fail, and builders will optimise for what the detectors see (declared colour pairs, listed synonyms, known duplicate shapes) while the scorecard reports zero. The answer is not to drop the contract form but to make the claim true: no LOCK row counts as checked until its check has caught a deliberately planted breach, the scorecard reports for each row whether that proof exists, and until then the charter describes itself as load-bearing in its rules and unproven in its enforcement.
